- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤-0.3) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes; if true outcome shows a sharp rise followed by a correction, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and shift peak later.  
- Model underestimates long-term trend (30d) when sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish; add 2–5% to forecast mean for 15–30d horizon if sentiment >0.5.  
- Model often lags true price by 1–3 days; if sentiment is trending upward, adjust forecast to align with 1–2 day ahead of true outcome.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (neutral), model tends to be flat; increase forecast volatility by 1–2% to reflect market uncertainty.  
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model delays reaction; forecast should rise 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change.  
- Model underestimates price in early 30d horizon if sentiment is weak; add 2–4% to first 5–7 days of forecast if sentiment <0.3.
